name: December 18, 2024 Franklin Fire Town Hall and Community Forum Special Meeting
agenda_text:
HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: The meeting will be live streamed at www.malibucity.org/video
  and via Zoom Webinar.

  HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
  submit email correspondence to citycouncil@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

  HOW TO PARTICIPATE IN-PERSON DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may
  speak during the meeting in-person.

  Malibu City Council
  Franklin Fire Town Hall and Community Forum
  Special Meeting Agenda

  Wednesday, December 18, 2024
  6:00 P.M. – CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING
  City Hall – Council Chambers
  23825 Stuart Ranch Road

To the members of the City Council of the City of Malibu:

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Mayor has called a Special Meeting of the City Council of the City of
Malibu to be held at Malibu City Hall, 23825 Stuart Ranch Road, Malibu, CA 90265, at 6:00 p.m. on Wednesday,
December 18, 2024, for the purpose of holding a town hall meeting regarding the Franklin Fire.

Six p.m.  Franklin Fire Town Hall Community Forum

  The City of Malibu and representatives from partner agencies will host a Community Town Hall
  and Community Forum to hear directly from the residents about the Franklin Fire and answer
  questions about fire response and recovery.

  Staff Contact: Deputy City Manager Brown, 456-2489, ext. 300

Adjournment

  Future Meetings

 Monday, December 23, 2024  CANCELLED  City Hall Council Chambers
 Monday, January 13, 2025  5:30 p.m. Regular City Council Meeting  City Hall Council Chambers
 Monday, January 27, 2025  5:30 p.m. Regular City Council Meeting  City Hall Council Chambers

  Guide to the City Council Proceedings and Decorum

 Role of the Presiding Officer: The presiding officer of the City Council, who shall be the Mayor, shall be responsible
 for maintaining the order and decorum of meetings. It shall be the duty of the presiding officer to ensure that these rules
 City Council Special Meeting Agenda  Page - 2 -  December 18, 2024

  of procedure and decorum are followed at all times. The presiding officer shall maintain control of communication
  between Councilmembers, between the Council and the public, and chair each meeting in a fair and impartial manner. It
  shall be the duty of each Councilmember to support the presiding officer in maintaining the order and decorum of Council
  meetings.

  Members of the Audience: Members of the audience shall not engage in disorderly or boisterous conduct, including
  clapping, whistling, stamping of feet, or other acts which disturb, disrupt, impede or otherwise disturb the orderly conduct
  of the City Council meeting. Persons addressing the City Council shall not engage in disorderly conduct which disrupts,
  or otherwise impedes the orderly conduct or Council meetings. Any person who so disrupts a Council meeting may, at
  the discretion of the presiding officer or a majority of the City Council, be subject to ejection from that meeting.

  City Council meetings are aired live and replayed on City of Malibu Government Access Channel 3 and are
  available on demand on the City’s website at www.malibucity.org/video. Copies of the staff reports or other written
  documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in the office of the City Clerk, Malibu City
  Hall, 23825 Stuart Ranch Road, Malibu, California, and are available for public inspection during regular office hours,
  which are 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Friday. Written materials
  distributed to the City Council within 72 hours of the City Council meeting are available for public inspection
  immediately upon distribution in the City Clerk's office at 23825 Stuart Ranch Road, Malibu, California (Government
  Code Section 54957.5.b.2). Copies of staff reports and written materials may be purchased for $0.10 per page.

  The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf (TDD),
  please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the Americans
  with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Environmental
  Sustainability Director Yolanda Bundy, (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable
  the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title
  II].

  I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
  in accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Special meeting agendas may be amended up to 24 hours in
  advance of the meeting. Dated this 17th day of December 2024 at 5:15 p.m.

  Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk

MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  SPECIAL MEETING
  FRANKLIN FIRE TOWN HALL AND COMMUNITY FORUM
  DECEMBER 18, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:00 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 6:07 pm. and Deputy City Manager explained
  ground rules for the Town Hall and how public comment would be conducted.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tern Marianne Riggins;  and
  Councilmembers Haylynn Conrad, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Joseph Toney, Assistant City
  Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin
  Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy, Environmental Sustainability
  Director; Maureen Tamuri, Interim Flaming Director; Susan Duenas, Public Safety
  Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Parker Davis, Media Technician; Christina
  Munoz, Deputy City Clerk; Jason Lawrence, Deputy City Clerk; Cynthia Alba, Executive
  Assistant; Barbara Esparza, Human Resources Technician; Matt Myerhoff, Media
  Information Officer; Caryn De La Cruz, Environmental Sustainability Analyst; Lauren
  Doyle, Contract Geotechnical Engineer; Andre Ketchedjian; Senior Plan Check Engineer;
  Rebecca Nelson-Brown, Senior Administrative Assistant; Tracey Rossine, Environmental
  Programs Manager; Tyler Eaton, Principal Planner; Larbi Azzaz, Assistant Planner; Sarah
  Flores, Emergency Services Coordinator; Brandie Ayala, Senior Management Analyst; and
  Travis Hart, Deputy Public Works Director

  PANELISTS: Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin; Drew Smith, Assistant Fire Chief Los
  Angeles Council Fire Department; Jennifer Seetoo, Captain Los Angeles COunty Sheriff s
  Department; Kevin McGowan, Director Los Angeles County Office of Emergency
  Management; Antonio Shelton, Superintendent Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School
  District; John Alford, Office of Congressman Brad Sherman; Sophia Soudani-John; Office
  of Supervisor Lindsey Horvath; CalFire Incident Management Team 4; California
  Department of Insurance; Ken Zimmer, Los Angeles County Public Works; and Bill
  Johnson, Los Angeles County Waterworks District No. 29

FRANKLIN FIRE TOWN HALL AND COMMUNITY FORUM

  The panelists introduced themselves and their agencies.

  The panelists answered questions and heard suggestions regarding:
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of December 18, 2024
  Page 2 of 2

  Vulnerable populations dependent on electrical power; emergency communications during
  power outages; evacuation zones; Public Safety Power Shutoff (PSPS) events; rooftop
  sprinkler systems; Community Brigades; evacuation notification systems; permits for
  generators; repopulation procedures and priorities; supplies for residents sheltering in place
  during disasters; AlertFM notification systems and radio communications; Pepperdine
  University’s shelter in place policy; Webster Elementary School repairs and backup power;
  brush clearance and defensible space; fire insurance and fire wise communities; electrical
  infrastructure and tire danger; Malibu Urgent Care; Community Emergency Response
  Team (CERT); responsibilities and resources for property owners and renters of a
  destroyed property; wildfire impacts on wildlife; air support for firefighting; evacuation
  warning sirens; debris removal; potential rockslides;

  Mayor Stewart presented closing remarks and announced that the Franklin Fire was 100%
  contained.

ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Stewart adjourned the meeting at 8:23 p.m.
